items.title: Medical devices given exceptional use authorisations
items.summary: Updated details on DEU/003/2026/001 in the attachment 'List of medical devices that are no longer covered by an exceptional use authorisation'.
items.meaning: These authorisations let named devices be supplied without the usual marking for a limited time, which changes what is available to a buyer.

items.title: Register medical devices to place on the market
items.summary: Updated the 2026/2027 Annual Fee information following completion of the fee recalculation. Added guidance for suspended accounts, including what to do if an Annual Fee has already been paid but the Annual Fee application has not been submitted in DORS.
items.meaning: This page sets who registers a device, and the fees, before it can be sold in the United Kingdom.

items.title: Clinical investigations for medical devices
items.summary: Added link to "Guidance on bringing software as a medical device to market".
items.meaning: This page affects companies gathering clinical evidence for a device in the United Kingdom.

items.title: MHRA sets out approach to strengthen patient and public involvement and engagement in medicines and medical device regulation
items.summary: New plan will broaden participation and make clearer how patient experience informs regulatory decisions, safety and innovation
items.meaning: A new official publication about the rules for supplying medical devices.

items.title: PPN 026: The social value model
items.summary: Added the document: Guidance on using PPN 026: The Social Value Model
items.meaning: This affects how social value is scored in central government tenders.

items.title: CE marked devices stay accepted in Great Britain long term
items.summary: On 21 October 2026 the government confirmed that Great Britain will keep accepting CE marked medical devices on a long-term basis. The UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) route continues alongside it.
items.meaning: A device already approved for the European Union market needs no additional UK approval route. Questions about a UKCA switch deadline for these devices now have a published answer.

sources.name: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)

items.title: European device database: 28 November 2026 registration deadline
items.summary: Four modules of the European database on medical devices (EUDAMED) have been mandatory since 28 May 2026. The European Commission gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register devices in its device module under the six month transition. Northern Ireland follows European Union rules.
items.meaning: This reaches companies supplying Northern Ireland or the European Union, including companies based in Great Britain. It does not replace registration with the MHRA for the Great Britain market.

sources.name: European Commission, device registration transition timeline
MHRA, medical devices in Northern Ireland

items.title: Device registration with the MHRA now carries an annual fee
items.summary: Since 1 April 2026 manufacturers are charged every year. From 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 the unit cost is £300 per year for each Level 2 category of the Global Medical Device Nomenclature (or Level 1 where there is no Level 2).
items.meaning: Keeping a range on the Great Britain register is now a recurring cost that grows with the number of device categories, and the unit fee changes each year.

items.title: Manufacturers must actively monitor devices already in use
items.summary: Post-market surveillance rules took effect across Great Britain on 16 June 2025. They apply to UKCA and CE marked devices placed on the Great Britain market after that date.
items.meaning: Performance concerns and incidents heard at customer sites feed a legal monitoring and reporting duty held by the manufacturer.

items.title: A national scoring standard for buying medical technology
items.summary: Guidance published on 11 June 2026 gives NHS buyers set questions and scoring criteria. The five value domains carry at least 60% of the weighting (social value at least 10%) and whole life cost no more than 40%.
items.meaning: Where a tender follows this guidance, most of the score rests on evidence of outcomes, efficiency, patient and staff benefit, supply resilience and social value, not purchase price alone.

sources.name: Department of Health and Social Care, national standard guidance

items.title: Wider carbon reduction plans for NHS suppliers from April 2027
items.summary: From 1 April 2027 procurements of £5 million a year or more (including VAT), and all new frameworks, need a 2027 carbon reduction plan covering scope 1, scope 2 and relevant scope 3 emissions. Lower value contracts above the procurement thresholds use the 2024 plan.
items.meaning: Bids for larger contracts and new frameworks started from that date are tested against the wider plan. Procurements begun before then stay on the earlier requirements.

sources.name: NHS England, 2027 carbon reduction plan requirements

items.title: New NHS Supply Chain frameworks ask for an Evergreen assessment
items.summary: Suppliers bidding for future NHS Supply Chain frameworks are required to submit an Evergreen sustainable supplier assessment and achieve Level 1 as part of the tender.
items.meaning: The assessment sits inside the framework tender itself, so a bid without Level 1 does not meet that requirement.

sources.name: NHS England, Evergreen sustainable supplier assessment

items.title: Health service buyers in England must assess modern slavery risk
items.summary: Regulations in force from 17 May 2026 require public bodies buying goods or services for the health service in England to assess modern slavery risk, and to take reasonable steps on any risk found.
items.meaning: Supply chain checks can appear in tender criteria and contract terms, including due diligence on subcontractors.

items.title: New social value model for central government buyers from January 2027
items.summary: Procurement Policy Note (PPN) 026 applies to central government procurements of £1 million or more started on or after 1 January 2027: at least 10% weighting below £5 million, at least 20% from £5 million.
items.meaning: It binds central government departments, their agencies and arm's length bodies. Other public buyers may choose to adopt it, so it does not by itself change every health service tender.

items.title: A national reimbursement route for a small number of health technologies
items.summary: The National HealthTech Access Programme, announced on 9 February 2026, expands technology appraisals by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) to devices, diagnostics and digital tools.
items.meaning: A small selection of high impact technologies can be reimbursed across the whole health service. It does not cover every product.

items.title: High cost device list nominations close at the end of May
items.summary: Nominations to add a device to, or remove it from, the high cost list are due by the end of May before the following year's NHS Payment Scheme. The 2026/27 scheme took effect on 1 April 2026.
items.meaning: Whether a device is paid for separately or inside the service price runs on a yearly cycle. Later submissions are not guaranteed to be considered until the following year.

items.title: Guidance on disclosing industry payments is due from government
items.summary: In its 18 December 2025 consultation response, the government said it will publish guidance on disclosing payments made by the medicines and medical devices industries to the healthcare sector.
items.meaning: For device companies this points to published best practice on which payments to report, in what format and how often, with a legal duty not chosen for now.

sources.name: Department of Health and Social Care, consultation outcome
